item.title: Inheritance and Donation Tax: Basel Countryside
item.description: How inheritance and gift taxes work in the canton of Basel-Country: rates, family exemptions and reporting procedures.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Inheritance and gift taxes are cantonal competence in Switzerland - In the canton of Basel-Country, rates and exemptions vary depending on the degree of kinship - Spouse and direct descendants benefit from favourable treatment - The declaration of succession must be submitted within the deadlines established by the canton
## Key facts - **What**: Inheritance and gift tax, managed at cantonal level - When: The declaration must be submitted within the deadlines set by Basel Countryside - Where: Canton of Basel-Country, North-West Switzerland - Who: Beneficiaries of inheritance or grantees according to the degree of kinship - Competence: Canton (not federal government) - Variability: Different rates for each Swiss canton
In the Swiss tax system, inheritance and gift taxes remain an exclusive competence of the cantons, not the federal government. This means that each canton has the right to establish its own rules, rates and procedures, generating significant differences between regions. In the canton of Basel-Country, as in the other 25 Swiss cantons, those who inherit property or receive a donation are subject to taxation according to specific cantonal rules.
The basis of the system is the degree of kinship of the beneficiary. Not all family members pay the same tax: the spouse of the deceased, direct descendants (children, grandchildren) and other relatives are treated at rates ### Rates and degree of kinship
In the canton of Basel-Country, as in the whole of Switzerland, the inheritance tax is structured in classes of beneficiaries, each with different rights and charges, according to the general intercantonal principles. Typical categories include:
**Spouse**: In most cantons, the surviving spouse is fully exempt from inheritance tax, recognizing that the remaining spouse should not see the assets available to continue life reduced. The exemption is usually complete, regardless of the amount of the inheritance.
Direct descendants: children, grandchildren and subsequent generations benefit from progressive rates that vary depending on the blood relationship. Direct children pay less than grandchildren; grandchildren less than great-grandchildren. The intention is to promote the transfer of assets within the close family unit. Many cantons also provide exemption thresholds for descendants, i.e. amounts below which no tax is levied.
Collateral relatives: brothers, sisters, cousins and more distant relatives face higher rates according to cantonal tax rules. The farther the kinship, the higher the tax increases, reflecting the idea that a stranger's inheritance is an economic event more distant from the beneficiary.
Non-relatives: beneficiaries without blood ties (friends, non-married institutions) face the maximum, often significant, rates.
These principles of ### How to Declare an Inheritance in Basel-Stadt Canton
When a person dies and leaves assets in Basel-Stadt Canton, the heirs or legal representatives (executor, administrator) must declare the assets to the cantonal tax office within the established deadlines. This process is mandatory and not optional.
**Step 1: Gather Documents** The executor or principal heir must collect all relevant documentation: death certificate, will (if present), inventory of assets, bank statements, securities, and previous tax returns of the deceased. The tax office of Basel-Stadt Canton will communicate exactly which documents are required at the time of opening the inheritance.
Step 2: Submit the Declaration on Time
The deadlines for declaring inheritance are set by the canton of Basel-Stadt, typically within 90 days of death or knowledge of death. Failure to respect the deadline entails penalties and late interest, making timeliness critical. The declaration can be submitted in paper form or, in many cantons, electronically through the tax administration portal.
Step 3: Valuation and Imposition
The tax office of Basel-Stadt Canton values the inherited assets based on the criteria established by the cantonal tax law. The valuation can be made at market value, cadastral value, or according to other methods provided by the regulations. Once the taxable amount is determined, the office calculates the tax due based on the applicable rates for the beneficiary.
Step 4: Liquidation and Payment
The tax office issues a tax notice (imposition notice) specifying the amount due. The heirs generally have a specified deadline to pay (usually 30-60 days from receipt). It is possible to request payment extensions or contest the imposition before the cantonal appeal authorities if the calculation is deemed incorrect.
### Critical Deadlines and Timelines
Each phase of the procedure is governed by rigid deadlines. Failure to meet deadlines for declaration, payment, or appeal entails increasing penalties. It is essential to contact the tax office of Basel-Stadt Canton promptly at the time of inheritance and clarify the specific deadline schedule applicable.
### Where to Turn
For precise information on current rates, exemption thresholds, deadlines, and declaration procedure in Basel-Stadt Canton, it is necessary to contact the cantonal tax administration directly. Specialized lawyers in tax law and notaries can also assist in the planning and declaration process, ensuring compliance with current regulations and maximizing available exemptions.
A trusted professional will guide you through the specific details of Basel-Stadt Canton, which vary from other cantons. Do not rely on general rules about the Swiss system: each canton has its own peculiarities. In 2021, Switzerland-EU relations were grey as an “elephant” in the middle of the road. Buying a home in the Basel-Country Canton almost always requires a mortgage. At the Swiss national level, the mortgage sustainability criteria follow common principles:
- LTV (Loan-to-Value) ratio: Swiss banks usually require a maximum mortgage-to-value ratio of around 80%, which means that the buyer must have at least 20% of the purchase price. - Repayment capacity: Banks assess the sustainability of the mortgage based on the borrower's income and other financial obligations. The purchasing procedure of a property in the Canton Basel-Landschaft follows standardized national Swiss steps, with cantonal specifics:
1. Search and offer: Identify the property and submit a binding offer to the seller. In Switzerland, there is no mandatory legal exclusivity period during the negotiation.
2. Preliminary (Vorvertrag): Once the offer is accepted, the parties sign a preliminary agreement that specifies the price, delivery date, and suspensive conditions, such as obtaining a mortgage.
3. Mortgage: Request a mortgage from the bank. The process includes property valuation, mortgage sustainability check, and signing the mortgage promise.
4. Notary: Once all details are finalized, the parties visit the notary to sign the definitive deed (Kaufvertrag). The notary registers the deed in the cantonal land register and calculates the transfer tax.
5. Property transfer: The notary registers the property transfer in the cantonal land register. At this point, the mortgage is disbursed, and the seller receives the payment.
### Transfer tax: timing and calculation
The transfer tax in the Canton Basel-Landschaft is calculated by the notary at the time of signing the definitive deed. It is a cantonal tax, meaning the rate and calculation methods are set by cantonal legislation, not federal law. The amount varies based on the purchase price and any applicable exemptions or benefits under cantonal laws, such as exemptions for the purchase of the primary residence in some cantons or reductions for spouses.
Typically, the transfer tax is paid at the time of signing the definitive deed by the notary or can be paid according to the modalities established by the canton.
### Notarial fees
Notarial fees in the Canton Basel-Landschaft are set by the notarial profession's tariff, not by federal law. They include: drafting the purchase deed, registration in the land register, legal advice, and administrative costs.
These fees are normally borne by the buyer (unless otherwise agreed with the seller) and represent, on average, 1-2% of the purchase price, depending on the complexity of the transaction.
### Additional costs: Registration fee and stamp duty
In addition to transfer tax and notarial fees, consider:
- Registration fee for the land register: A cantonal tax for registering the property in the land register.
- Valuation costs: If required by the bank for the mortgage.
- Property insurance: Mandatory if the mortgage exceeds a certain threshold. It covers property damage (fire, theft, etc.).
All these costs should be factored into the purchase planning to avoid liquidity shortfalls in the final phase.
### Final checklist before purchase
Before proceeding with the purchase, it is advisable to verify:
- Mortgage sustainability (LTV ratio, repayment capacity)
- Availability of own funds (at least 20% of the purchase price)
- Cantonal transfer tax estimate
- Notarial fee estimate
- Annual fiscal burdens as a property owner
- Property insurance coverage
Seeking the advice of a real estate consultant or notary for reviewing these aspects is highly recommended, especially if it is the first time purchasing a property in Switzerland.

A key feature of the L permit is the constraint on the employer and the canton of employment specified in the initial application. The L permit is structured for temporary and short work needs. The 12 months of validity are non-negotiable: any initial request cannot exceed this period. Renewal is not automatic. The employer must submit a new application at least 30 days before the expiry of the current permit. If this request is not submitted, the permit expires and the worker loses the right to stay and work in Switzerland. It is the responsibility of the employer (with the support of the cantonal authorities) to manage administrative time to avoid interruptions.

The extension of the L permit depends on administrative and economic factors. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### How to request the L permit: step-by-step procedure The L permit request starts with the employer, not the employee. Phase 2: Submission of the request to the canton. The employer submits the file to the competent cantonal authority in Basel-Country responsible for work permits (usually the Migration Office or Population Office). SEM intervenes in a consultative capacity for non-EU/EFTA citizens.

For those who live and work in Switzerland, the change will bring significant practical benefits. The offline payment system is not an absolute novelty. Sweden has been using it for years, responding to concerns about the resilience of digital infrastructure during critical outages. Countries such as Finland, Norway and Estonia are introducing similar measures.
With this mission statement, Switzerland becomes the first Central European country to adopt a widely shared and coordinated solution to strengthen the resilience of electronic payments. According to the Federal Department of Economics, the Swiss approach is distinguished by the consensus reached between the public sector (Federal Council, SNB) and the private sector (business representatives).
### Concrete implications for merchants and customers
Owners of small and medium-sized Swiss stores will be able to continue to cash out even when the telecommunications network is interrupted — a guarantee of sales continuity in the event of an emergency. Customers will not have to fear being cut off from their payments during a blackout.

### 3-level tax structure in the canton of Basel-Country The tax system of the Canton of Basel-Country is structured on three levels of taxation: the direct federal tax (IFD) paid to the Confederation and managed by the Federal Tax Administration (AFC), the cantonal tax administered by the regional tax office, and the municipal tax collected by the individual municipalities of the canton according to a fixed multiplier on the cantonal tax base. Each level applies progressive rates on the various brackets of taxable income, determined after the application of deductions allowed by federal legislation and specific cantonal provisions. Taxpayers resident in the canton are obliged to submit an annual tax return within the deadlines set by the cantonal administration, indicating income from employment and ### Practical implications for residents of the Canton of Basel-Country Those who reside in the canton of Basel-Country and receive income from any source are subject to taxation at all three levels: federal, cantonal and municipal. The total annual tax burden therefore depends both on the cantonal rate set by regional legislation and on the multiplier applied by the municipality of residence. Taxpayers with the same income but residing in different municipalities of the canton of Basel-Country will pay different municipal taxes, sometimes to a significant extent. For this reason, it is useful to check the municipal multiplier of your municipality and calculate the total tax burden starting from the net tax base after all allowable deductions. A preliminary estimate before the declaration makes it possible to organise the payment and assess the effect of additional deductions (e.g. voluntary payments to the third pillar 3a) on the net tax due.
### Differences between declaration of employees and independent workers Employees have income taxed directly by the employer, who pays tax advances according to cantonal calendars (usually monthly or quarterly). The cantonal tax administration verifies the payment of advances and settles the differences at the end of the tax year. Self-employed persons and business owners must submit a complete declaration with accounting annexes and detailed administrative management,
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Procedure step-by-step for the cantonal tax declaration For those residing in the Canton Basel-Landschaft and required to submit the annual declaration, the process follows these concrete steps:
**Phase 1: Collecting documentation** — Gather pay slips received, bank statements, AVS/LPP payment receipts, professional expense justifications (if self-employed), LAMal/KVG premium payment attestations during the year, documentation of donations to recognized institutions, bank account statements and investment records if subject to wealth taxation.
Phase 2: Authentication on the online portal — Reach the official website of the cantonal tax administration and authenticate with personal credentials (federal social insurance number + password, or digital signature via Swiss e-banking). The portal is available in German and French; informative texts, downloadable forms, and guides are available in Italian at the counters or upon request.
Phase 3: Filling out the declaration — Enter gross income, deduct documented expenses, indicate AVS/LPP payments made, LAMal premiums paid, and other allowed deductions. The system automatically calculates the cantonal and communal tax based on the net taxable income and applicable legislation.
Phase 4: Attaching justifications — Digitally upload required documents (pay slips, receipts, bank statements) within the file size limit set by the portal.
Phase 5: Submission and confirmation — Submit the digitally signed declaration. The portal generates a receipt with the date and time of submission; a copy remains archived in the personal account.
Phase 6: Monitoring the status — Periodically access the portal to verify the evaluation status and receive communication of the result (tax due, refund, or zero payment).
### Terms of delivery and administrative contacts The ordinary deadline for submitting the cantonal declaration is typically set between April and May of the following year of income; exact deadlines are communicated by the cantonal tax administration in documents sent to the taxpayer and visible on the official online portal. Extensions are granted upon motivated request submitted within the set terms. For clarifications on specific cantonal tax rates, allowed deductions in the canton, technical issues with accessing the portal, or other administrative matters, it is possible to contact the cantonal administration's counters in the detached capitals, the dedicated phone number for tax support (retrievable from the official website), or the email service of the tax office for non-urgent communications.
### Fiscal planning tools and tax estimates Many taxpayers use online calculators provided by federal entities (AFC) or the canton itself, where they can enter gross income and receive an accurate estimate of the total tax due (federal + cantonal + communal). This tool allows them to evaluate the concrete effect of additional deductions (third pillar 3a voluntary payments to a third-party pillar, professional pension contributions) on the net tax due and plan in advance for payment. Conscious fiscal planning enables taxpayers to avoid end-of-year surprises and identify legitimate opportunities for reducing their tax burden in compliance with federal and cantonal legislation.

## In a nutshell - Cantonal inheritance tax in the canton of Basel-City: variable rates by degree of kinship - Significant exemptions for spouse and direct descendants — progressive rates for distant relatives - Compulsory declaration within deadlines established by the cantonal administration - Procedure via official forms at the tax office: contact for updated details
## Key facts - **What**: Cantonal tax on hereditary successions and donations in the Canton of Basel-City - Where: Canton Basel-City (BS), German-speaking Switzerland - Who: Heirs, legatees and donors second degree of kinship - Type: Cantonal tax (non-federal) — varies from canton to canton in Switzerland - Base: Degree of kinship — the closer the bond, the lower the rate - Exemptions: Surviving spouses and direct descendants enjoy a subsidized regime
The inheritance and gift tax in the Canton of Basel-City is a cantonal tax that affects the transfer of assets free of charge, both by inheritance and by donation. Unlike [imposta federale diretta, che è uniforme in tutta la Svizzera](nav:calculator), inheritance and gift taxes are governed entirely by cantonal laws: each Swiss canton has its own tax regimes, with rates and exemptions defined by its own legislation.
In the Canton of Basel-City, as in all cantons, the tax is divided according to the degree of kinship between the deceased (or donor) and the heir (or donor). The closer the relationship ### Rates, exemptions and degrees of kinship in the Canton Basel-City
In the Canton of Basel-City, as in the rest of Switzerland, taxation is divided into stages according to the degree of kinship. The main grades are organized as follows:
**First Degree (Spouse and Children)**: The surviving spouse generally benefits from substantial tax protection. In many Swiss cantons, including the Canton of Basel-City, the spouse enjoys a total exemption or a significantly reduced rate. Similarly, children and direct descendants benefit from very low rates or partial exemptions, reflecting their order of priority in Swiss civil law.
Second degree (parents, brothers, sisters): Relatives in the second degree of kinship are subject to moderate rates, higher than those reserved for the spouse and children, but lower than those of the most distant degrees.
Third grade (grandparents, uncles, cousins) and higher grades: These subjects benefit from an even higher rate. Persons without kinship (friends, acquaintances, strangers) are subject to the maximum rates provided for by cantonal law.
To consult the exact rates applicable in the Canton of Basel-City, it is essential to contact the cantonal tax administration directly, as these rates may be subject to legislative changes and vary not only by degree of kinship, but also by amount brackets.

If you have been appointed as an heir or have received an inheritance in the City of Basel, you must follow a formal procedure to fulfill your tax obligations. Here are the main steps to follow:
Phase 1: Gather Essential Documents
Obtain the following documents: - Original will (if exists) or certificate of intestate succession - Death certificate of the deceased (extract from the register) - Documents related to the inherited assets (bank statements, stock certificates, real estate deeds, insurance policies) - Documentation regarding debts or liabilities of the inheritance (mortgages, credits, funeral expenses) - Marriage or birth certificates to prove the degree of kinship
Phase 2: Contact the Cantonal Tax Administration
Contacting the City of Basel's tax office is a crucial step. Reach out to the administration to: - Request the official forms for the inheritance declaration - Clarify the submission deadlines (usually within a few months of the death, but verify exactly) - Obtain specific information on the applicable tax rates for your degree of kinship - Understand if you are entitled to exemptions or reliefs
Phase 3: Complete the Inheritance Declaration
Fill out the official form, providing: - Personal details of the deceased (name, date of death, last residence) - Complete list of heirs and legatees with indication of the degree of kinship - Detailed inventory of all assets (active and passive) - Market value of each asset at the time of death - Total value of the inheritance and taxable base
**Phase 4: Submission and Payment**
Submit the declaration within the specified deadline at the cantonal tax office (in person, by mail, or through the digital platform, as indicated by the administration). The office will notify the amount of tax due based on the applicable tax rate for your degree of kinship. Payment must be made within the terms indicated in the notification.
### Deadlines and Terms for Declaration
The deadlines for the inheritance declaration in the City of Basel vary depending on the current cantonal legislation and must be verified with the tax administration, as they may be subject to changes.
In general: - The declaration must be submitted within a few months of the death (the exact deadline varies - contact the office to confirm) - [The notification of the amount due follows after the submission of the declaration](nav:tax-return) - The tax payment must be made within the deadline indicated in the notification - Failure to comply with the deadlines may result in administrative penalties, interest, and potential coercive recovery procedures
Therefore, it is essential to act promptly and contact the tax administration as soon as possible after the death.
### When to Seek Professional Help
Given the complexity of the matter and the variability of inheritance situations, it may be advisable to consult specialized professionals: - Notary: for issues of will validity, interpretation of the testator's will, and succession law - Tax consultant or accountant: for accurate tax calculation, form completion, and tax planning - Lawyer specializing in succession law: for disputes between heirs or complex legal issues - Cantonal administration: for clarification on tax rates, exemptions, deadlines, and updated forms

## In a nutshell - Opening a business requires a choice of legal form (company, SA, SAGL, simple company) - Compulsory registration in the commercial register of the canton of Basel-City - Social contributions (AVS/AI 10.6%, AD 1.1%, LAMal) mandatory immediately - Federal, cantonal and municipal taxes in three levels
## Key facts - **What**: Registration in the trade register for new economic activities - Where: Canton of Basel-City (cantonal administration) - Who: Individual entrepreneurs, partners, shareholders according to legal form - When: Before starting economic activity - Legal forms: Sole proprietorship, simple company, SA, SAGL, cooperative - Taxes: Three-level system — federal (IFD), cantonal, municipal - Compulsory contributions: AVS/AI 10.6%, AD 1.1%, private LAMal, LPP if employees
Opening a business in the canton of Basel-City means facing an administrative and fiscal system structured on three levels of taxation and numerous social security obligations. The initial choice concerns the legal form: the tax regime, minimum capital requirements and insurance charges vary significantly between sole proprietorships, partnerships, public limited companies (SAs) and limited liability companies (SAGS).
The first concrete step is the registration in the commercial register of the canton of Basel-City. It is not an optional requirement: every economic activity exercised in a professional capacity must be registered before ### The Swiss tax system: three levels
Taxation in Switzerland consists of three distinct levels: direct federal tax (DFI), cantonal tax and municipal tax. Basel City, as a semi-canton, has its own cantonal multipliers and Basel municipalities apply municipal multipliers on a cantonal basis. This means that two businesses with the same turnover in different municipalities of Basel City can pay slightly different amounts of municipal tax, although the federal and cantonal basis remains identical.
A **SA** will pay corporate net income taxes at the three levels according to the federal progressive rates, the cantonal rate of Basel City and the specific municipal multiplier. A sole proprietorship will pay personal professional net income taxes, reducing the tax base with deductions for mandatory social contributions (AVS/AI, unemployment insurance) and documented professional expenses. A SAGL combines elements of both: the entity is taxed on income, but with greater distributional flexibility than an SA.
### Social security and insurance obligations
Health insurance (LAMal) is mandatory for anyone residing in Switzerland and must be taken out within 3 months of the start of residence or the start of business for those who already reside. LAMal is not a tax or a salary contribution: it is a private insurance with per capita premiums that vary by canton and sick fund. Basel
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Step-by-Step Procedure for Registration
**Phase 1: Preliminary Preparation**
Before contacting the commercial register, define the legal form of your activity. If you choose a sole proprietorship, you will need a business name (denomination), the company address (Swiss address), and a brief description of the activity. If you choose a SA or SAGL, you must draw up a statute or founding deed, designate administrative bodies (board of directors, manager), and pay the minimum capital to a bank (depositary trustee). The simple partnership requires a written agreement between partners.
Phase 2: Registration with the Cantonal Office
The canton of Basel City has a central office for the commercial register where you can submit the registration application. At the national level, information on uniform procedures is coordinated between cantonal administrations, but the actual request is made to the cantonal office. Typical documents include: - Completed registration form (available at the cantonal office) - Bank certificate (if capital payment) - Statute/founding deed (for SA, SAGL, simple partnership) - Designation of administrators and legal representatives with authenticated signature - Identity document of the applicant
Phase 3: Notification to Tax and Insurance Authorities
After registration with the commercial register, the Federal Administration of Customs and Taxes (AFC) automatically receives the data from the cantonal database. However, you must notify your cantonal residence of the tax situation (federal and cantonal declarations) and conclude health insurance within 3 months. If you have employees, you must also register the company with the competent administrative office for professional pension management (LPP) for your sector and canton.
Phase 4: Opening a Bank Account and Accounting
Open a bank account in the company's name (SA/SAGL) or in your name (sole proprietorship). If your activity has invoiced above a certain limit, you may need to request a VAT number from the AFC for invoicing and paying the value-added tax. The accounting must be regularly updated and kept for at least 7 years for potential tax audits.
### Deadlines and Recurring Obligations
After registration, annual obligations include: - Federal and cantonal tax declarations: within the terms set by the AFC and canton (typically spring/summer of the following year) - Payment of AVS/AI, AD contributions: according to the calendar of the Commercial Register Office and cantonal administration - Payment of LPP contributions (if employees are registered): monthly to the company's pension fund - Balance sheet declaration (for SA, SAGL; less stringent for sole proprietorship): within 6 months of the end of the year - LAMal renewal and annual verification of cantonal subsidies
### Tools for Calculating Your Tax Burden
Use the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) to simulate the impact of different levels of gross income and see how the withholding system (AVS, AD, federal and cantonal taxes) affects the net available. This simulation helps understand if the overall cost structure is sustainable.
To understand the context of living costs in the canton of Basel City and Switzerland in general, consult the guide on [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living). Remember that each canton has margins of maneuver on cantonal tax rates, and common ones apply their own multipliers.
For details on [pension and retirement](nav:pension), consult the guide dedicated to AVS/LPP calculations for self-employed workers. For [health insurance](nav:health), check the updated LAMal premiums in your canton and the conditions for subsidies.
Next step: Contact the Commercial Register Office of Basel City for the updated registration form, or consult a tax advisor familiar with local fiscal dynamics. Initial investment in a brief consultation will save you costly errors in administration and tax declarations.
